info.name: Express Task API
info.description: Swagger-aligned, guided individual demonstrations. Select the supplied environment and read postman/README.md before running state-changing requests. Do not run the whole collection blindly.

request.description: Public endpoint. Expected: 200 and a simple server-running message.
Public health check. Expected: 200.
Returns the same OpenAPI specification used by Swagger UI. Expected: 200 YAML.
Public demonstration endpoint. Send example JSON; inspect the echoed body in the 200 response.
Extra documentation request: returns the Swagger UI HTML. For the interactive view, open this URL in a browser.

exec: pm.test('Swagger UI is served', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.include('Express Task API Documentation'); });

request.description: Creates a disposable user and profile. Requires a unique userEmail; clear both runId and userEmail to generate a fresh test address. Expected: 201. Saves userId and targetUserId. Use a real accessible mailbox instead if demonstrating email reset.

exec: if (pm.response.code !== 201) { throw new Error("Request failed; saved variables were not changed."); }

request.description: Sign in the disposable user with userEmail and userPassword. Expected: 200. Saves userToken, userId and targetUserId; a fresh signin replaces the stored token.

exec: if (pm.response.code !== 200) { throw new Error("Request failed; saved variables were not changed."); }

request.description: Enter the seeded administrator credentials in adminEmail and adminPassword first. Expected: 200. Saves adminToken and adminUserId. This is another example of the Swagger signin operation.

exec: if (pm.response.code !== 200) { throw new Error("Request failed; saved variables were not changed."); }

request.description: STATE CHANGE. Requires userToken. Expected: 200. Invalidates this user’s existing access tokens; sign in again before protected requests.

Requires a real accessible email in userEmail and configured SMTP. Expected: generic 200 whether or not an eligible account exists; it does not prove delivery. Missing SMTP gives 503. Check the actual mailbox.

exec: pm.test('Reset request is accepted or email is not configured', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 503]));

request.description: Copy only the token parameter from the emailed link to passwordResetToken and set newPassword. Expected: 200 with a valid unused unexpired token. Changes the password and invalidates old JWTs; update userPassword and sign in again.

Requires passwordResetToken from an email link. Expected: 200 HTML for a correctly shaped token; this GET checks only token format, not expiry or prior use. Open the email link in a browser to see the form.

STATE CHANGE. Requires passwordResetToken from the email and newPassword. This sends URL-encoded form fields. Expected: 200 HTML with a valid unused unexpired token; 400 HTML on invalid token/password. Update userPassword and sign in again.
STATE CHANGE. Requires a previously deactivated disposable account and its current userEmail/userPassword. Expected: 200; sign in again to receive a token.
Requires a fresh userToken. Expected: 200 with safe account fields.
STATE CHANGE. Requires userToken, current userPassword and a different newPassword. Expected: 200. Old tokens become invalid; update userPassword and sign in again.
STATE CHANGE. Requires userToken and current userPassword for a disposable account. Expected: 200; the profile remains. Reactivate and sign in again. Last active admin returns 409.
IRREVERSIBLE. Requires userToken and current userPassword. Use only a disposable account. Expected: 204 with no body; profile and reset-token records cascade. Last active admin is protected.
Requires a fresh userToken from Authentication → Sign in. Expected: 200; observe data.profile.
Requires a fresh userToken from Authentication → Sign in. Expected: 200; observe data.profile. STATE CHANGE: updates the supplied displayName and bio.

Requires a fresh adminToken from Authentication → Sign in as admin. Expected: 200. The targetUserId must identify another disposable user, not the admin. Default example lists the first 20 users; edit query parameters to demonstrate search, role or status.
Requires a fresh adminToken from Authentication → Sign in as admin. Expected: 200. The targetUserId must identify another disposable user, not the admin.

exec: pm.test('Security fields are absent', () => { const user = pm.response.json().data.user; pm.expect(user).not.to.have.property('passwordHash'); pm.expect(user).not.to.have.property('tokenVersion'); });

request.description: Requires a fresh adminToken from Authentication → Sign in as admin. Expected: 200. The targetUserId must identify another disposable user, not the admin. STATE CHANGE: example promotes a normal user to admin and invalidates their old tokens. To demote later set role to user; repeat same role returns 409.

Requires a fresh adminToken from Authentication → Sign in as admin. Expected: 200. The targetUserId must identify another disposable user, not the admin. STATE CHANGE: target must be active. Existing target tokens are invalidated.

Requires a fresh adminToken from Authentication → Sign in as admin. Expected: 200. The targetUserId must identify another disposable user, not the admin. STATE CHANGE: target must be deactivated. Target needs to sign in again.

Requires a fresh adminToken from Authentication → Sign in as admin. Expected: 200. The targetUserId must identify another disposable user, not the admin. IRREVERSIBLE: only target a disposable account. Expected: 204; related profile and reset-token records are deleted.

item.name: Experiments
item.description: Run experiments individually after the prerequisites in postman/README.md. Some change account data.

item.name: GET /api/v1/users/me — Experiment 1 - Missing token returns 401
item.description: Question: what happens when a protected endpoint receives no Bearer token? Expected: 401 Unauthorized.

request.description: Experiment: inspect the HTTP response and Test Results. See postman/README.md for prerequisites and the required order; some experiments depend on an earlier state change.

item.name: GET /api/v1/admin/users — Experiment 2 - Normal user gets 403 on admin route
item.description: Question: the token is valid, but its user role is user. Expected: 403 Forbidden because identity is valid but permission is insufficient.

request.description: Experiment: inspect the HTTP response and Test Results. See postman/README.md for prerequisites and the required order; some experiments depend on an earlier state change.

exec: pm.test('Authenticated normal user is forbidden', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

item.name: POST /api/v1/auth/signup — Experiment 3 - Signup cannot assign admin role
item.description: Question: can a public caller promote themselves by adding role to signup? Expected: 400 Bad Request; signup input is strict.

request.description: Experiment: inspect the HTTP response and Test Results. See postman/README.md for prerequisites and the required order; some experiments depend on an earlier state change.

exec: pm.test('Public role assignment is rejected', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(400); pm.expect(pm.response.json().success).to.eql(false); });

item.name: PATCH /api/v1/users/me/profile — Experiment 4 - Profile rejects unsupported fields
item.description: Question: can profile editing change account permissions? Expected: 400 because role is not a profile field.

request.description: Experiment: inspect the HTTP response and Test Results. See postman/README.md for prerequisites and the required order; some experiments depend on an earlier state change.

exec: pm.test('Unsupported profile field is rejected', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

item.name: PATCH /api/v1/users/me/profile — Experiment 5 - Set profile bio baseline
item.description: Set a bio so the next request can test PATCH omission. Expected: 200 and the new bio is returned.

request.description: Experiment: inspect the HTTP response and Test Results. See postman/README.md for prerequisites and the required order; some experiments depend on an earlier state change.

exec: pm.test('Bio baseline is saved', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const bio = pm.response.json().data.profile.bio; pm.expect(bio).to.eql(`Bio baseline ${pm.environment.get('runId')}`); pm.environment.set('profileBioBefore', bio); });

item.name: PATCH /api/v1/users/me/profile — Experiment 6 - Omitted bio stays unchanged
item.description: PATCH only displayName and omit bio. Expected: the saved bio is unchanged; omitted is different from null.

request.description: Experiment: inspect the HTTP response and Test Results. See postman/README.md for prerequisites and the required order; some experiments depend on an earlier state change.

item.name: PATCH /api/v1/users/me/profile — Experiment 7 - Null clears bio
item.description: Send bio: null. Expected: 200 and profile.bio becomes null.
